To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a polyprotein containing the Pol domain is associated with the membrane-bound replication complex of ToRSV.
the RNA-dependent RNA Polymerase of Tomato ringsort virus (ToRS) associates with the membrane-bound replication complex in a polyprotein form.

the RNA-dependent RNA Polymerase of Tomato ringsort virus associates with the membrane-bound replication complex in an intermediate form of a polyprotein that contains domains for the proteinase and genome-linked viral protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of membrane targeting of viral replication proteins.
the identification and localization of the viral proteins involved in replication and assembly of Tomato ringspot nepovirus.
the identification of the domains of ToRSV proteins involved in membrane targeting and the elucidation of the mechanism of targeting of viral proteins to the site of viral replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VPg-Pro-Poly' is a truncated polyprotein that is associated with ER-derived viral membranes and is a component of the replication complex.
VPg-Pro-Poly' is a truncated version of a 111kDa polyprotein that is peripherally associated to the ER-derived membranes active during viral replication.
VPg-Pro-Poly is a truncated version of VPg-Pro-VPg-Pro-Pol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NTB, VPg, Pro, and Pol of ToRSV are all targeted to the replication complex via interactions with a viral membrane-targeted protein.
the domains for NTBs, VPg and Pol are targeted to ER-derived membranes by virtue of their interaction with a viral protein that is associated with these membranes.
a viral membrane protein is involved in the targeting of the viral replicase to the site of viral replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the viral membrane protein is a good target for antiviral strategies.

the Pol domain of ToRSV does not target to membranes on its own, but is brought to the ER membrane in association with other viral proteins, in a manner similar to that reported for the Pol of the related nepovirus, Grapevine chrome mosaic virus.
the RNA-dependent RNA replication of ToRSV occurs in association with a subpopulation of ER-derived membranes.
